newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N.'s Foa to leave her post at end of year.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Foa to leave her post at end of year.

text.p: Sylvana Foa, the popular wise-cracking chief U.N. spokeswoman, said on Monday she would leave her post at the end of the year when Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali ends his term.

"Despite all the fun, it is really time for me to go off and do something new, try something new in my life like be in love, write a book, enjoy things a little bit," she told her regular noon briefing.
She said she had spoken to Kofi Annan, who will take over as secretary-general Jan. 1, that she would be available for short, special missions.
She said her deputy, Ahmad Fawzi, would take over in the new year until Annan makes a decision on the post.

Foa, an American, said she had a one-year leave of absense from the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees to take the job as Boutros-Ghali's spokeswoman and would ask UNHCR for an unpaid leave of absense for another year.

"I've talked to Kofi and said I dont know how long I can sit on the beach and I am available if he ever needs someone for a mission," she said. "So maybe you will be seeing me somewhere at some point."

Foa, a former foreign editor and journalist for United Press International, became a favourite of correspondents because of her irreverance, blunt comments and willingness to tackle the U.N. bureaucracy for news.
